message.text: The new decision, and AGENTS.md's Three reviews before ready (line 204), change how the comparison record decides which findings are real. A Sonnet agent writes the defect list, any finding that a later commit fixed with a failing test first "counts as real", and only findings raised on the first reviewed head are counted. At base the rule is different. A finding is valid only when the maintainer adjudicates it with `melian compare adjudicate` (comparison-with-external-reviewers.md, Adjudication; evals.md, Comparisons). Shadow retirement counts "each pull request once across rounds", and "an unadjudicated finding counts as pending, never guessed". The head decision has no `Supersedes:` or `Amends:` line for either of those base texts, so the head picks its own standard for measuring the reviewers.

After that head nothing changes. Each fix pass gets a Melian round, and the rules for when Codex's review and the review of record run again stand.

After the merge, the coordinator has a Sonnet agent write the pull request's defect list for its comparison record: each distinct defect a reviewer raised on the first reviewed head, who raised it, and the commit that fixed it or the builder's answer disputing it. A finding that a later commit fixed, with a failing test first, counts as real. The coordinator spot-checks a sample.

## Why

- The fix commits are an answer key nobody has to write. AGENTS.md already requires a failing test before a fix, so a fixed finding was a real defect at the head the test failed on.
- All three reviews already run, so the comparison costs only the defect list, about a dollar a pull request.
- Starting the three together is faster than running them in turn.
- Ten such pull requests are also the window [the shadow retirement rule](2026-10-06-shadow-retirement-merged-window.md) asks for, measured on like for like.

## What it costs

- A defect one reviewer finds is no longer fixed before the next reviewer runs, so two reviewers may report it. The comparison record already counts a defect once however many report it.
- The first round reviews a head no review has improved, so it may raise more findings than a first round does today.
- Only the first head is compared. Later rounds on fix commits stay uncompared, as they are now.

explanation.whyHere: Whether a finding gets fixed depends on the review process being measured, not on whether the finding is valid. Melian's own status forces the fix: an acknowledge or block finding keeps `melian/review` from passing until it is fixed or dismissed through a host round (AGENTS.md step 5). The review-of-record brief tells builders to "Fix each finding", and fixing is cheaper than asking the coordinator or the maintainer to settle a dispute. Under this rule, a finding counts as real because the builder followed the gate. That inflates the precision and recall of the reviewer whose findings gate the merge. Those numbers feed the shadow retirement rule (recall 0.75 over ten pull requests), which decides whether Codex's review is retired. Counting only the first head also leaves out every valid finding a shadow raises on a fix-pass head, though base counts all rounds.

properties.failureScenario:
A pull request's first reviewed head gets a Melian round with an acknowledge-level `design` finding. Suppose it is noise, for example a hypothetical gap that no caller reaches. AGENTS.md step 5 does not let the builder queue while acknowledge findings stand unread, and a block-level finding needs a fix or a host-round dismissal. So the builder writes a test that pins the current behaviour, makes a two-line change and pushes it. After the merge, the Sonnet agent follows line 17 / AGENTS.md:204: the finding was fixed with a failing test first, so it is listed as a real defect. Melian's precision for that pull request reads 1.0 where the maintainer would have judged the finding noise.

The reverse case: on fix pass 2, Codex's review flags a valid defect that the first-head reviews all missed. The rule says "Only the first head is compared", so the defect is never counted. Codex gets no recall credit and Melian is not charged a miss, though the base retirement rule counts each pull request across all its rounds.

Over the ten-pull-request window, Melian's recall against the shadows can reach 0.75 on a sample that the gate itself shaped. The maintainer would then be asked to retire Codex's review on numbers no adjudication produced. Base said "an unadjudicated finding counts as pending, never guessed".

# The three reviews run first on one head

Status: ruled by the maintainer on 2026-11-27, in the coordinator's session. The coordinator proposed it; the maintainer asked for the draft and agreed its text that day.

## Problem

Every pull request gets Codex's adversarial review, a Melian round and the Claude review of record. AGENTS.md ran them one after another: Codex first, then its fixes, then a round, then its fixes, then the review of record. Each reviewer saw different code. A defect Codex found was fixed before Melian's round ran, so the round could neither find it nor miss it.

Example: the maintainer's parity loop needed to know which defects each reviewer finds. For the three pull requests it measured, [#613](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/613), [#619](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/619) and [#623](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/623), the coordinator had to run each reviewer again, blind, on one old head, and build each defect list by hand. About forty pull requests merged between 2026-11-04, the date of the newest comparison record, and 2026-11-27 with all three reviews posted and nothing that could compare them.
